description: Say which role this token holds, its ticket and stage, the tools it may call, the documents it may write and its limits. Use first when unsure what you may do; for a ticket's state use get_ticket.
name: whoami

outputSchema.description: What a token is and what it may do.

role.description: What a caller may do: one ticket in one stage, the board, or everything.

description: Read a ticket's fields, state, its documents' names and versions and its latest activity, without document text. Use when starting work or judging one ticket; for a document's text use read_document, for older history list_activity.

ticket_id.description: The ticket, such as CF-12. A run may leave it out: it has one ticket.

name: get_ticket

outputSchema.description: A ticket as an agent starts on it. Document text comes from `read_document`.

items.description: A document as a ticket's index lists it: no text.

name.description: The documents a ticket can have, in the order they are written.

items.description: One appended record of a ticket's history; `id` rises with every append.

ticket.description: A ticket as the board shows it, with the column its facts put it in.

column.description: A board column, in the order a ticket walks them.

state.description: The state of a ticket's pull request as the forge reports it.

description: List tickets in board order with column, priority, labels, blocked state and branch, filtered by column, label, parent or repository. Use to decide what to work on or find a ticket; for one ticket's detail use get_ticket.

anyOf.description: A board column, in the order a ticket walks them.

parent.description: Only the children of this ticket.

name: list_tickets

items.description: A ticket in a list: enough to choose one.

column.description: A board column, in the order a ticket walks them.

description: Create a ticket under the next number. A run files a follow-up for something found on the way (a few per run); the owner files any ticket. Use when new work should go on the board; for an existing ticket use update_ticket.
name: create_ticket

column.description: A board column, in the order a ticket walks them.

description: Change named fields of a ticket (title, type, description, labels, priority, assignee, due, blocked, rank, tests, links), its branch, or archive it, checked as the board checks them and recorded in its activity. Use when a ticket's card should say something else; the column follows the branch and pull request.

branch.description: Set it; an empty string clears it.

anyOf.description: An edit: only the fields given change.

name: update_ticket

outputSchema.description: A ticket after an update and the fields that changed.

description: List a ticket's activity newest first (moves, documents, runs, checks, answers, notes, findings), filtered by kind. Use to see what happened and why work was sent back; get_ticket has only the latest few.

ticket_id.description: The ticket, such as CF-12. A run may leave it out: it has one ticket.

name: list_activity

outputSchema.description: A page of a ticket's history; `next_cursor` continues it, `None` at its end.

items.description: One appended record of a ticket's history; `id` rises with every append.

description: Record a note on a ticket's activity under your name; the owner reads it. Use to leave a finding that is not a change to any field. A diagnosis (why work is stuck) is for the owner and coordinator.

kind.description: diagnosis is for the owner and coordinator.

ticket_id.description: The ticket, such as CF-12. A run may leave it out: it has one ticket.

name: post_note

outputSchema.description: A note that was recorded: the activity record's id.

description: Read one ticket document (requirements, spec, uat, mock, review, notes) as text, a page at a time; next_offset continues it. Use when you need what a document says; get_ticket lists which exist and their versions.

name.description: The documents a ticket can have, in the order they are written.

ticket_id.description: The ticket, such as CF-12. A run may leave it out: it has one ticket.

name: read_document

outputSchema.description: Part of a document's text; `next_offset` continues it, `None` at its end.

name.description: The documents a ticket can have, in the order they are written.

description: Replace a document with the whole text (name the version you read, none to create it) or append to it. The text is checked for its kind and refused with the line numbers when wrong. Use to write your stage's output; a run may write only its stage's documents.

base_version.description: The version you read; none to create. Not for append.

name.description: The documents a ticket can have, in the order they are written.

ticket_id.description: The ticket, such as CF-12. A run may leave it out: it has one ticket.

name: write_document

outputSchema.description: A write that was taken: the document's new version.

name.description: The documents a ticket can have, in the order they are written.

description: Dismiss a review finding you do not agree with, with the reason; the reviewer and the owner read it on the ticket. Use when a finding is wrong or out of scope; to fix one, change the code instead. A finding is dismissed once.

finding_id.description: A finding id such as F2.

reason.description: Why it does not apply, 1 to 1000 characters.

ticket_id.description: The ticket, such as CF-12. A run may leave it out: it has one ticket.

name: dismiss_finding

outputSchema.description: A finding a Build run dismissed, with the reason it gave.

description: List questions with their choices and answers, by status (open by default), for one ticket or, for the owner, all. Use to see what waits on the owner or what was decided; answer_question takes a question's id.

ticket_id.description: A run: its own. The owner: leave out for every ticket.

name: list_questions

outputSchema.description: A page of questions by id; `next_cursor` continues it, `None` at its end.

items.description:
A question an agent asked the owner.

`index` is its position among the ticket's questions of the same document, which is how the
app addresses it.

anyOf.description: One answer to a question; the current one is the newest.

items.description: One choice a question offers; `ticked` is set on the picked ones of an answered question.

description: Answer a question by its id with the choices picked or with words; picks win over words. An answered question is refused unless replace is true. Use when the owner has decided what a question asks.

answer.description: Words, when no choice is picked.

name: answer_question

outputSchema.description: The answer to answering: `text` is the question's, `answer` the words recorded.

description: Search the owner's standing rules, decisions and lessons; every word of the query must match and an empty query lists them all. Use before asking or acting on a guess, to learn what is already decided; to record a lesson use propose_memory.

query.description: Words that must all match; empty lists all.

name: search_memory

items.description: An entry in a search: what to do, why, and what guards it.

description: Propose a lesson: what to do now, why (what went wrong), the guard that now prevents it and the paths or tests it is about. It is held until the owner approves it. Use when a mistake that could recur has been fixed; search_memory finds what exists.

guard.description: The test that now prevents it, if any.

scope.description: Who loads it; empty loads for everyone.

name: propose_memory

outputSchema.description: A proposal that was recorded: it is held until the owner approves it.
